title: Forget ChatGPT — 10 Under-the-Radar AI Tools Doing the Real Work in 2026
partialText:
A hand-tested list of the best new AI tools for 2026 — underrated picks to automate and grow your small business before everyone else catches on.

You already know ChatGPT. So does everyone else — which means there’s no edge left in it.

The best new AI tools of 2026 are the ones still flying under the radar: fresh, lesser-known tools quietly running real work for the small businesses that found them early. I test these for a living, and a few of them genuinely made me sit up.

Here are 10 under-the-radar AI tools worth grabbing right now — what each does, why it’s different, and exactly how a small business can put it to work this week.

1. Granola — the meeting notes that take themselves

No awkward bot “joining” your call. Granola listens in the background, writes clean notes for you, and turns every meeting into a searchable memory you can actually find later. Use it for: never losing a client commitment buried in scattered notes again.

2. Fyxer — an AI assistant that runs your inbox

It sorts your email, drafts replies in your own tone, and writes the follow-ups — users say it hands back about an hour a day. Works inside Gmail and Outlook. Use it for: clearing the inbox that quietly eats your every morning.

💡 Want the full list?

I keep a free, hand-curated directory of the best AI automation tools — updated every month: AI Automation Tools → Prefer it in your inbox? Subscribe to the newsletter.

3. Clay — how modern teams find leads on autopilot

Clay pulls data from 100+ sources and runs an AI research agent (“Claygent”) to find, enrich, and personalize prospects at scale — the not-so-secret weapon behind a lot of sharp outreach right now. Use it for: building a targeted prospect list without the manual digging.

4. Gumloop — “Zapier crossed with ChatGPT”

Drag-and-drop automations that wire your apps to an AI model, no code. Teams at Shopify and Webflow already lean on it. One of the most underrated tools on the market this year. Use it for: automating the research, data cleanup, and content tasks that swallow hours.

5. Julius AI — chat with your spreadsheets

Upload your data, ask a question in plain English (“which months were my best?”), and it writes the analysis, runs it, and hands you charts and answers. No formulas, no analyst. Use it for: real business insight from your own numbers, in minutes.

6. Manus — the agent that actually does the task

Most AI waits for your next prompt. Manus plans the steps and executes — it researches, compiles, builds, and comes back with finished work while you do something else. Use it for: handing off a whole research or admin job and walking away.

7. Lovable — describe an app, get an app

Type what you want in plain English and it builds a working website or web app — front end, back end, deploy and all. No developer required. Use it for: spinning up an internal tool or a landing page in an afternoon.

8. OpusClip — turn one long video into ten viral shorts

Feed it a webinar or podcast; it finds the highest-retention moments and cuts captioned, platform-ready shorts for Reels, Shorts, and TikTok. Use it for: a month of social content from a single recording.

9. Vapi — an AI receptionist that answers your phone

A natural-voice agent that takes inbound calls, books appointments, and qualifies leads — 24/7, no human on the line. Use it for: capturing the after-hours callers you’re currently sending to voicemail.

10. PhotoRoom — studio-grade product photos in seconds

Snap a phone photo; it removes the background and generates clean, professional product shots and brand visuals — what used to take a designer ten minutes, done instantly. Use it for: e-commerce listings and social posts without a photographer.

Here’s the thing about AI right now: by the time a tool is famous, the edge is gone. The advantage goes to whoever finds the good ones first.

That’s the whole reason I keep a free, hand-curated directory of fresh AI tools — updated every month, so you don’t have to dig through Product Hunt at midnight:

Want the new ones delivered instead of hunted? Subscribe to the newsletter — a short monthly drop of tools actually worth your time.

For the record: none of these paid to be on this list — they’re just genuinely good.
